capability: Shrink a mark step by step until it still reads
title: Shrink it through the gates.

hook.picture: Close on the whale proudly holding a detailed mark full of fine lines. It drops the mark into a tiny tab square and it becomes a grey smudge.
hook.words: Looks great on the big screen.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: Our logo turns to mush as a tiny icon.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: founder looking at the browser tab

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: the same detailed mark shrunk three times, faster each time. Each shrink loses the fine lines all at once, never by choice.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: Shrinking throws away the wrong details.

stakes.body: The brand vanishes exactly where people see it most: tabs, phones, feeds.

solution_hint: Remove one thing at a time. Check each.

metaphor.body: Five gates along the line, each smaller than the last. At each one the mark drops one detail by choice, and a ring checks it still reads at tab size.

steps.picture: The mark passes the first gate and drops one detail, a thin fin line, by choice.
At each gate a ring checks the mark at tab size. It glows, and the mark drops the next detail.
steps.words: Each step must still read when tiny.
steps.sound: Pluck per gate, stepping down in tune.

steps.picture: Push-in: at gate four the whale drops the eye. The ring shows it no longer reads as a whale and the gate closes. The eye goes back and a fin goes instead.
steps.words: Lose the wrong part? The gate says no.
steps.sound: A sour clunk, then the pluck in tune.

steps.picture: Gate five: one single stroke that still reads as the whale. The tab-size ring glows.

real_case.claim: Glyph Foundry's README lists a Saul Bass 5-rung reduction ladder ending at a 16px cut; the studio README adds a 4-test emblem gauntlet (favicon, silhouette, one-move, cut-out).

honest_limit.picture: The single stroke passes every gate and reads crisply at tab size, but a new viewer names it a wave, not a whale. Readable is not the same as recognised.
honest_limit.words: It reads. But it reads as something else.

not_this.body: Readable at any size is not recognisable.

ending_pattern.body: The whale drops the mark into the same tiny tab square as in FELT, and this time the one-stroke mark stays crisp. The pod answers ✓.
ending_pattern.callback: Same tab square and drop gesture as bar 2, the smudge replaced by a crisp stroke.

end_belief.body: Shrink on purpose, one step at a time.

beats.words: Looks great on the big screen.

beats.words: On a tab, it's just a smudge.
beats.sound: The chord collapses to a muddy hum.

beats.camera: Still z 1.6, half bar of stillness

beats.sound: Problem motif: a chord squeezed into a hum.

beats.picture: Two more jumps, faster, every 1 beat then half. Each one smears a different part.
Motion stops. Five gate outlines ghost along the line, each smaller.
beats.words: Remove one thing at a time. Check each.

beats.picture: Gate five: one single stroke that still reads as the whale. The tab-size ring glows.
Wide: the five steps laid out left to right, from full mark to one stroke.
beats.words: Real run: a ladder borrowed from Saul Bass.

beats.picture: Four small rings test the last stroke: tab, shadow, one move, paper cut-out. All four tick.
beats.words: Four tests at the smallest size.

beats.picture: Slow push to the pod's 'wave' chip.
beats.camera: One slow push to the thing that slipped

beats.picture: FELT framing: the whale drops the mark into the tiny tab square again. This time the single stroke sits crisp.
beats.camera: Close z 1.6, the FELT framing restored

beats.picture: The pod glancing at the tab answers ✓. The whale sparks.
beats.sound: Chord resolves from the single note.

beats.picture: The five steps fading behind the tab, the whale breathing.
beats.words: Shrink on purpose, one step at a time.

score_self.reason: A concrete, visual pain everyone has seen. The step-down mechanism draws easily, the limit is pictured and fair, and the case numbers are on the card. Weakest is the second case beat, four tests in one beat.
